name: _test_serialization_subcmul
description: Elementwise ``self - alpha * other`` with NumPy-style broadcasting, exercised on same-shape pairs, broadcast pairs (including an expanded zero-stride operand) and non-broadcastable shape pairs. ``alpha`` is a Scalar (schema default 1) exercised as int (0, -3, 5, torch.iinfo(dtype).max), finite float (0.0, -1.5, 2.5), special float (nan, inf, -inf), a large float boundary (1e30) and complex 1 + 2j, the complex value only with complex operands. Operand dtypes come from the pytest's float, int and complex lists: float16/float32, int8/uint8/int16/int32 and complex64 are always included, while bfloat16, float64, int64 and complex128 are added only when ``utils.bf16_is_supported``, ``utils.fp64_is_supported`` or ``utils.int64_is_supported`` is set. The suite also covers mixed-dtype promotion pairs, non-contiguous/transposed, storage-offset and expanded layouts (with operand-unchanged checks), zero-element operands, and autograd through ``torch.autograd.grad`` over both operands with the resulting gradients compared against the native reference, including broadcast and complex (alpha=1 + 2j) rows. Negative rows require the candidate to raise for non-broadcastable shapes, a bool ``self``, non-numeric ``alpha`` (tensor, string, None, list), non-tensor ``self``/``other`` and a missing operand; the pytest calls the candidate positionally throughout. Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_test_serialization_subcmul(Tensor self, Tensor other, Scalar alpha=1) -> Tensor. Original Gems pytest owns the full contract: overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation must not be narrowed to this representative signature. Registered schemas: aten::_test_serialization_subcmul(Tensor self, Tensor other, Scalar alpha=1) -> Tensor.
